scope: Incremental iOS 16 alignment: RC9 module isolation, UI integration, fork handshake, file and directory signature collection backports.

supported_matrix.scope: All iOS 16.x firmware and device combinations actually supported by RC9 3.0.7 RootHide jailbreak paths.
supported_matrix.clarification: This does not mean every device can jailbreak every iOS 16.x release. MinimumOSVersion 16.0 is not proof that the full jailbreak matrix has been validated.

rules: Do not raise RC9's minimum iOS version above 16.0.
Preserve all iOS 16.x firmware/device combinations supported by RC9's existing 3.0.7 RootHide jailbreak paths, not only the user's iPadOS 16.5 device.
Maintain an explicit iOS 16.x firmware, device/chip, exploit, and offset matrix; distinguish source-derived support from device-validated combinations.
Do not infer jailbreak support for every iOS 16.x release or device from the app's MinimumOSVersion of 16.0.
Only port upstream behavior that is available and correct on iOS 16.
Exclude behavior requiring iOS 17 or later; when a newer API is optional, require an iOS 16 fallback and an explicit availability guard.
Review every upstream API and ABI change against iOS 16 before implementation.
validation: Both app Debug and Release deployment targets remain 16.0.
The full RC9 iOS 16.x version/device/exploit/offset support matrix is inventoried and validation evidence is tracked per combination.
Device acceptance is recorded on the user's iOS 16 hardware separately from CI.

excluded_whole_tree_baselines.reason: Not the RootHide comparison branch; do not replace the RootHide runtime tree with it.

checks: Runtime policy regression tests including macOS native fake-mount mock
limitations: Not an iOS device acceptance test.
Workflow reported a cache-save warning although the run completed successfully.

reference_comparison.finding: Neither reference contains RC9's user-managed fake-mount path list or settings API. zqbb's internal fakelib mount is a separate boot and userspace-reboot mechanism.

backports.scope: Per-call pipe ownership, checked raw I/O, EINTR retry, EOF rejection, SIGPIPE suppression, failed-child exit and parent cleanup/reaping.
backports.preserved: Existing RootHide systemhook hook installation and Mach fork-fix protocol.
backports.limits: No proof of all inherited-descriptor lifetimes, post-fork configuration locks, or iOS device behavior.

backports.scope: Tri-state adhoc collection, parse/hash failure propagation, checked growth and partial-output cleanup.
backports.preserved: RC9 Cryptex/TrollStore filtering, per-file randomized hashes, errno-style statuses and existing consumer checks.
backports.limits: Not the full upstream trustcache_fs walker, signature attachment, randomization rollback, parser-submodule, or kernel trustcache lifecycle audit.

phase_four.scope: Propagate directory open/read/stat/allocation/parse/callback/close failures, reject partial collections, probe Mach-O magic with EINTR and short-read handling, and clean up all add-entrypoint outcomes.
preserved: File collector path filtering and per-slice randomization.
Recursive toggle and no symlink or special-file traversal.
All UI, low-power scheduling, mount configuration and injection policy.
limitations: No other active in-tree callers of these exported directory-add APIs were found; not a confirmed root cause for reboot or UI symptoms.
The new native harness uses real host filesystem operations but mocks ChOma parsing, file hash collection and kernel insertion.
Does not provide a transaction across concurrently changing files or roll back earlier per-file randomization.
Kernel trustcache reader lifetime and remaining signature attachment/parser paths remain open.

phase_five.scope: Default injection mode, optional manager installation and existing verbose-log switch audit.
phase_five.preserved: Existing whitelist file and user choices are not deleted, rewritten or forcibly disabled.
phase_five.unresolved: No group-member device evidence establishes which component created their user whitelist file. RC9 has no matching optional Sileo installation entry yet.

phase_six.scope: Injection policy cache snapshots, concurrent readers and fork child state.
changes: Publish a fresh per-process cache state after fork without touching an inherited lock or XPC snapshot.
Read each config through one descriptor and verify device, inode, type, size, mtime and ctime remain stable.
Retry interrupted reads and avoid publishing short or concurrently modified file contents.
Preserve the prior valid snapshot during invalid or transient reads; clear it when the path is removed or is no longer a regular file.
preserved: Per-call-site cache structure rather than ZQBB's global LRU.
Injection mode selector, blacklist/whitelist precedence and config keys.
RC9 iOS 16 deployment target, UI, low-power and custom-mount features.

native_harness_cases: same-size content change with restored mtime
invalid intermediate content preserves previous valid snapshot
fork child reads while inherited parent cache lock is held

limitations: Host XPC parser and unfair lock are test doubles.
No iOS arm64/arm64e device acceptance yet.
vfork semantics, all post-fork lock lifetimes and repeated-fork child memory lifetime remain under review.
A persistently invalid config keeps the last valid policy until a valid update or path removal.

ledger.evidence: The three app storage methods have unchanged bodies; only their compilation unit and UI import changed.

scope: JBServer argument, DATA and FD bounds

ledger.evidence: Existing behavior is preserved; no equivalence or extraction is claimed in phase one.
The official and zqbb reference commits contain no user-managed path list or settings API; method bodies remain identical to the RC9 baseline.
ledger.distinction: zqbb's internal fakelib mount is a boot and userspace-reboot mechanism, not the RC9 user-configured mount feature.

ledger.evidence: Keep the existing candidate layout pending device acceptance; no new bounce or rendering changes.
